newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks stay higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks stay higher at midday.

text.p: A rally in bonds, a surge in banking stocks and a follow-through on yesterday's strength in high techs kept Wall Street stocks higher in midday trading.
The Dow Industrials were up 54 points, or 0.85 percent, at 6401 after having set off the NYSE's automatic curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 1025 EST/1525 GMT.

The action shifted back to blue chips today, as investors felt encouraged by General Electric Co's plan to boost the quarterly dividend, increase the share repurchase program and split the common stock two-for one.

Big Board advances led declining issues by 15 to eight on volume of about 247 million shares. The Nasdaq Composite Index, which on Wednesday outperformed the Dow, was up seven points, or 0.57 percent, at 1293. U.S. Treasuries were higher, with the long bond up 19/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
GE was one of the prime movers of the Dow Industrials, rising two points to 101.

"The action is in the blue chips after the General Electric announcement," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Yesterday was a big day for Nasdaq, but Nasdaq stocks are still doing okay overall."

"The high techs are following up on their rally from yesterday as are the biotechs. Banks are up because rates are stable," Bleier said. "It seems that all is well with the world after a brief but volatile pause."
But he said he doubted the Dow Industrials would make much headway beyond their old intraday high at 6410 and that most investors were aware of this.
"The correction we saw last week and the week before generally see a snapback rally to test old highs," he said."
Intel Corp was up 2-7/8 at 138-5/8 and Microsoft Corp was up 2-1/8 at 84-3/4.

American Home Products Corp was up 7/8 at 59-7/8. Among the banks, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc was up 1-3/4 at 97-5/8, Chase Manhattan Corp was up 2-1/4 at 89-1/2, Citicorp was up two at 103 and BankAmerica Corp was up 1-3/4 at 100-1/8.
Among today's losers was Micro Warehouse Inc, down 7-9/16 at 12-7/16 and topping the Nasdaq most active list.
The company said it expected fourth quarter profits to fall sharply below analysts' estimates, citing a fall in gross margins and increased competition in the Macintosh business.
Macintosh is made by Apple Computer Inc.
Among today's special situations, shares of LCI International Inc were down 4-5/8 at 20-7/8 and topped the NYSE most active list.
Shares of Nike Inc were up six at 61-1/8. Hambrecht & Quist raised fiscal year 1997 earnings per view estimates to $2.80 from $2.55 and increased FY98 estimates to $3.35 from $3.04.
Robertson Stephens raised its fiscal year 1997 EPS view to $2.80 from $2.62 and its 1998 EPS view to $3.80 from $3.50.
